title: Nodal algebraic-space morphisms on etale charts and after base change
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A scheme morphism is nodal of relative dimension one if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is pure of dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension] and has only smooth points [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and ordinary nodes. Over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], an ordinary node is a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] with completed local $\Omega$-algebra $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. This scalar-compatible scheme condition is [def-sfb-scheme-nodal-relative-curve]; the completed local algebras use the canonical structural scalar map [def-trf-completed-local-scalar-map]. Define $f$ to be nodal of relative dimension one if there exists a commutative diagram $U\to V$ over $X\to Y$ with $U,V$ schemes, both vertical morphisms representable etale [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism], $U\to X$ surjective, and $U\to V$ nodal of relative dimension one. This condition is equivalent to requiring $U\to V$ nodal in every such diagram, without requiring surjectivity in the universal condition. It is also equivalent to requiring $X\times_YV\to V$ nodal for one surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$, and to requiring $f\circ p$ nodal for one representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$. Nodal morphisms remain nodal under every algebraic-space base change $Y'\to Y$, with fibre products as in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. In particular these equivalences apply to restrictions to arbitrary source open subspaces [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Pointwise on a geometric fibre, on locally finite type scheme charts over its algebraically closed ground field [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the condition of being smooth of relative dimension one or an ordinary node is preserved and reflected by etale scheme charts; the completed local ring at a geometric closed point can be computed on such a chart. No properness, nonemptiness, connectedness or global equidimensionality hypothesis is imposed on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0DSG (lemma-nodal-local), conditions (4)--(7), and Tag 0DSF (lemma-base-change-nodal); definition-nodal-family and its preceding paragraph. The geometric point interpretation is the etale-local test used in curves.tex lemma-node-etale-local and lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source.

proof.text: Write $N$ for the scheme condition in the statement, tested on every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. This agrees with the test on the chosen geometric fibres of [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. One direction is a special case. Conversely, if $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ lies over $s$, choose a $\kappa(s)$-embedding $k=\overline{\kappa(s)}\subseteq\Omega$; then $C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the base change of $C_{\bar s}$ along $k\subseteq\Omega$. If $C_{\bar s}$ is pure of dimension one, every local dimension of this locally finite type $k$-scheme is one, so every irreducible component of the base change has dimension one by [lem-trf-field-extension-component-local-dimension]. Every nonsmooth point of the base change has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ by [lem-trf-node-algebraically-closed-extension], and is closed by [lem-trf-nodal-point-etale-locality] applied to the identity. Stability under scheme base change follows: flatness and local finite presentation persist by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). For $T\to S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, associativity identifies $(C\times_ST)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. This is the identical $\Omega$-scheme tested in the hypothesis, including empty fibres, so purity, smoothness and the completed local $\Omega$-algebra condition persist.

proof.text: There always is a chart diagram with surjective left vertical arrow: choose an atlas $V\to Y$, then an atlas $U\to X\times_YV$. Their projection $U\to X$ is surjective etale. The two nodes [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] supply the products, their scheme representability when both entries are schemes, and etale composition and pullback. Now suppose $h:U\to V$ is a nodal witnessing chart and $h':U'\to V'$ any chart. Put $R=U\times_XU'$ and $W=V\times_YV'$, both schemes. The maps $R\to U$, $R\to U'$ and $W\to V$, $W\to V'$ are etale; $R\to U'$ is surjective. By [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-source-locality], $R\to U\to V$ is nodal (apply source locality to the family consisting of the identity of $U$ and $R\to U$). It factors through $R\to W$. Reflection in [lem-sfb-scheme-nodal-etale-postcomposition] for $W\to V$ makes $R\to W$ nodal; preservation for $W\to V'$ makes $R\to V'$ nodal. Source locality along $R\to U'$ now makes $h'$ nodal. Conversely the universal condition applies to the first atlas diagram. For scheme $X,Y$, the identity diagram also shows that the space condition agrees with the scheme condition.

source.place: Tag 0DSG (lemma-nodal-local), (6) and (7); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ proof, common refinement

proof.text: For any scheme map $B\to Y$, put $P=X\times_YB$. With $U,V,h$ a witnessing diagram, set $R=U\times_YB$ and $C=V\times_YB$. These are schemes by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The map $R\to C$ is exactly the scheme base change of $h$ along $C\to V$, hence nodal by step 1. The diagram $R\to C$ over $P\to B$ has etale vertical arrows, and $R\to P$ is surjective, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. It witnesses nodality of $P\to B$. For an arbitrary space map $Y'\to Y$, choose an atlas $B\to Y'$ and then an atlas $A\to X\times_YB$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The preceding witness for $X\times_YB\to B$, together with the universal-chart criterion of step 2, makes $A\to B$ nodal. The source map factors as $A\to X\times_YB\to X\times_YY'$. Its first arrow is the chosen atlas and its second is the pullback of $B\to Y'$, so their composite is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The target arrow $B\to Y'$ is the chosen atlas. Thus this is a witnessing diagram for the arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 0DSF (lemma-base-change-nodal); Tag 0DSG (4), construction on pulled-back charts

proof.text: Consequently nodal $f$ pulls back to a nodal map over every target atlas. Conversely, if $P=X\times_YV\to V$ is nodal for a surjective etale atlas $V\to Y$, choose an atlas $A\to P$. The universal criterion for $P\to V$ makes $A\to V$ nodal, while $A\to X$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. This is a witness for $f$. For a source atlas $p:U\to X$, nodal $f$ makes $fp$ nodal: in every chart $A\to B$ over $U\to Y$, the composite $A\to X$ is etale by the same node, so step 2 applies to $f$. Conversely a witness $A\to B$ for $fp$ has $A\to U$ surjective etale, hence $A\to X$ surjective etale; it witnesses $f$. These arguments apply to any chosen atlas, including empty atlases of empty spaces.

An open subspace $O\subset X$ is representable by open immersions by [def-a1-space-open-subspace]; pulling a witnessing source chart back to $O$ gives an open subscheme of that chart. The inclusion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and the source-locality lemma used in step 2 preserves nodality on it. Hence all the proved criteria apply to source restrictions. Now let $e:D\to C$ be an etale map of locally finite type $\Omega$-schemes, as between etale scheme charts of a geometric fibre $X_\Omega$ (no purity of dimension is assumed for $C$), with $y\mapsto x$. Smoothness at a point is preserved and reflected by [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness]. For the relative dimension, apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] to $e$ and $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: $\dim_yD=\dim_y(D_x)+\dim_xC$, and $\dim_y(D_x)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; so $\dim_yD=\dim_xC$ and smoothness of relative dimension one at $y$ and at $x$ agree. A closed point of a locally finite type $\Omega$-scheme is maximal in an affine finite-type chart, so its residue field is $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]. Hence if $x$ or $y$ is an ordinary node, the hypothesis of [lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso] holds, so both points are closed with residue field $\Omega$ and the actual induced map $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,y}$ is an isomorphism; thus ordinary nodes are preserved and reflected, and the same node computes the completed local ring at any geometric closed point. Two charts through the same geometric point have the etale scheme common refinement furnished by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], so both computations agree via that refinement. This gives the asserted chartwise meaning of the completed geometric local ring without choosing a preferred chart.

Define $f$ to be nodal of relative dimension one if there exists a commutative diagram $U\to V$ over $X\to Y$ with $U,V$ schemes, both vertical morphisms representable etale [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism], $U\to X$ surjective, and $U\to V$ nodal of relative dimension one. This condition is equivalent to requiring $U\to V$ nodal in every such diagram, without requiring surjectivity in the universal condition. It is also equivalent to requiring $X\times_YV\to V$ nodal for one surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$, and to requiring $f\circ p$ nodal for one representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$. Nodal morphisms remain nodal under every algebraic-space base change $Y'\to Y$, with fibre products as in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. In particular these equivalences apply to restrictions to arbitrary source open subspaces. Pointwise on a geometric fibre, the condition of being smooth of relative dimension one or an ordinary node is preserved and reflected by etale scheme charts; the completed local ring at a geometric closed point can be computed on such a chart. No properness, nonemptiness, connectedness or global equidimensionality hypothesis is imposed on $X$ or $Y$.
